answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit before offering services, with the stake slashed on verified fraud. Like a glacier that moves slowly yet crushes everything in its path, the deposit makes mass fake identities expensive to create and slow to wander into new markets. Reputation then grows gradually, the way a lotus opens petal by petal, so a fresh identity cannot instantly outrank established agents. Attackers pay real cost per identity while honest agents keep cheap, steady access.
